newsitem.title: USA: KEDO seeks to buy resid fuel for North Korea.
newsitem.headline: KEDO seeks to buy resid fuel for North Korea.

text.p: The Korean Peninsula Energy Development Organization (KEDO) has issued a purchase tender for 42,000 metric tonnes of residual fuel oil for late January or early February delivery to North Korea, the company said in a statement Friday.

The tender asks for maximum two percent sulphur material, with approximately 20,000 metric tonnes for discharge at Nampo, Songrim or Sonbong, North Korea, and approximately 22,000 metric tonnes for discharge at Sonbong.
Bids are due by 1000 EST Wednesday, January 22, at the offices of KEDO agent International Services Corp in Washington, D.C.
KEDO, an international organization established to implement nuclear non-proliferation in North Korea, has agreed to supply the country with 500,000 tonnes of fuel oil annually.
